mcqs.q: If you've flipped a fair coin and got heads 5 times in a row, what is the probability the next flip is heads?
options: 1/2 — each flip is independent of the previous ones.
7, because you do 12 / 2 = 6 and then add 3 with the multiplication symbol meaning 'and'.
1 because the coin has clearly been biased by the previous flips.
Less than 1/2, because the coin is 'due' to land on tails to balance the results.

mcqs.q: Is P(A | B) the same as P(B | A)?
options: Generally no — these conditional probabilities are different unless P(A) = P(B).
P(A | B) = P(B | A) because conditioning is symmetric.
1 because the coin has clearly been biased by the previous flips.
P(A | B) is always P(A) + P(B).
1 because the coin has clearly been biased by the previous flips.
2, because in BIDMAS multiplication comes before division (12 / 6).
18 — division and multiplication share the same precedence; work left to right (6 x 3).
7, because you do 12 / 2 = 6 and then add 3 with the multiplication symbol meaning 'and'.
